claim: DetecDiv is a microfluidic-based image acquisition platform combined with deep learning-based software for high-throughput single-cell division tracking.
source: Here, we have developed DetecDiv, a microfluidic-based image acquisition platform combined with deep learning-based software for high-throughput single-cell division tracking.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the developed platform.

claim: DetecDiv can automatically reconstruct cellular replicative lifespans with high accuracy.
source: We show that DetecDiv can automatically reconstruct cellular replicative lifespans with high accuracy and performs similarly with various imaging platforms and geometries of microfluidic traps.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental validation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: DetecDiv performs similarly with various imaging platforms and geometries of microfluidic traps.
source: We show that DetecDiv can automatically reconstruct cellular replicative lifespans with high accuracy and performs similarly with various imaging platforms and geometries of microfluidic traps.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments with different trap designs and imaging systems shown in Figure 3.

claim: DetecDiv provides comprehensive temporal cellular metrics using time-series classification and image semantic segmentation.
source: In addition, this methodology provides comprehensive temporal cellular metrics using time-series classification and image semantic segmentation.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the various classification models described in the manuscript.

claim: DetecDiv can be applied to automatically quantify the dynamics of cellular adaptation and real-time cell survival upon exposure to environmental stress.
source: Last, we show that this method can be further applied to automatically quantify the dynamics of cellular adaptation and real-time cell survival upon exposure to environmental stress.
evidence: This is demonstrated through hydrogen peroxide stress experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Budding yeast mother cells undergo about 20–30 asymmetric divisions before entering senescence and dying.
source: In budding yeast, mother cells undergo about 20–30 asymmetric divisions before entering senescence and dying (Mortimer and Johnson, 1959).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by Mortimer and Johnson, 1959.

claim: Budding yeast has become a reference model for understanding the fundamental mechanisms that control longevity.
source: Over the last decades, this simple unicellular has become a reference model for understanding the fundamental mechanisms that control longevity (Denoth Lippuner et al., 2014; Janssens and Veenhoff, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Several independent mechanistic models have been proposed to explain entry into replicative senescence, including asymmetric accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs).
source: Several independent mechanistic models have been proposed to explain entry into replicative senescence, including asymmetric accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs) (Sinclair and Guarente, 1997), protein aggregates (Aguilaniu et al., 2003), signaling processes associated with loss of vacuole acidity (Hughes and Gottschling, 2012), or loss of chromatin silencing (Pal and Tyler, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies proposing different mechanisms.

claim: Classical replicative lifespan (RLS) assays by microdissection have been decisive in identifying and characterizing genetic factors and pathways that influence longevity in budding yeast.
source: Classical replicative lifespan (RLS) assays by microdissection, combined with genetic perturbations, have been decisive in identifying and characterizing genetic factors and pathways that influence longevity in budding yeast (McCormick et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to McCormick et al., 2015.

claim: How the appearance of markers of aging is coordinated temporally and causally remains poorly understood.
source: However, how the appearance of markers of aging is coordinated temporally and causally remains poorly understood (Dillin et al., 2014; He et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations indicating gaps in current understanding.

claim: RLS assays by microdissection generally give no information other than the replicative age upon cell death.
source: In part, this is due to the difficulty of directly characterizing the sequence of events that constitute the senescence entry scenario: RLS assays by microdissection generally give no information other than the replicative age upon cell death
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of traditional methods based on established knowledge of the technique.

claim: Old cells enrichment techniques ignore the well-known large cell-cell variability in the progression to senescence.
source: old cells enrichment techniques ignore the well-known large cell-cell variability in the progression to senescence, which may blur the sequence of individual cellular events.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of enrichment techniques based on known biological variability.

claim: The development of microfluidics-based mother cell traps has allowed continuous observation of individual cell divisions and relevant fluorescent cellular markers under the microscope from birth to death.
source: Based on pioneering work in yeast (Ryley and Pereira-Smith, 2006) and bacteria (Wang et al., 2010), the development of microfluidics-based mother cell traps has partially alleviated these limitations by allowing continuous observation of individual cell divisions and relevant fluorescent cellular markers under the microscope from birth to death (Lee et al., 2012; Xie et al., 2012; Fehrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies using microfluidic devices.

claim: Monitoring individual cells over time in a microfluidic device has demonstrated the unique potential to quantitatively characterize the heterogeneity in cellular dynamics during aging.
source: In these studies, monitoring individual cells over time in a microfluidic device has demonstrated the unique potential to quantitatively characterize the heterogeneity in cellular dynamics during aging.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the cited studies on microfluidic devices.

claim: Recent years have seen a wide diversification of microfluidic devices aimed at improving both experimental throughput and cell retention rates.
source: Recent years have seen a wide diversification of microfluidic devices aimed at improving both experimental throughput and cell retention rates (Jo et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2015; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent developments in microfluidic technology.

claim: New microfluidic developments have helped to highlight the existence of independent trajectories leading to cell death.
source: These new developments have helped to highlight the existence of independent trajectories leading to cell death (Li et al., 2017; Morlot et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020) and to better understand the physiopathology of the senescent state (Neurohr et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies using improved microfluidic devices.

claim: The difficulty of extracting quantitative information in an efficient and standardized manner due to the manual aspect of the analysis is a key problem associated with high-throughput time-lapse imaging.
source: However, the hype surrounding these emerging microfluidic techniques has so far masked a key problem associated with high-throughput time-lapse imaging, namely the difficulty of extracting quantitative information in an efficient and standardized manner due to the manual aspect of the analysis (Huberts et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huberts et al., 2014.

claim: Lifespan analyses require manual division counting and frequent corrections in cell segmentation.
source: Yet, in practice, this is out of reach since lifespan analyses require manual division counting and frequent corrections in cell segmentation.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of current analysis methods.

claim: The rapid development of powerful deep learning-based image processing methods in biology using convolutional neural networks (CNN) suggests a way to overcome the technical barrier of manual analysis.
source: Fortunately, the rapid development of powerful deep learning-based image processing methods in biology using convolutional neural networks (CNN) (Laine et al., 2021) suggests a way to overcome this important technical barrier.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review on deep learning methods in biology.

claim: A previous study showed the potential of image classification by a CNN or a capsule network to classify the state of dividing yeast cells trapped in a microfluidic device.
source: Recently, a study showed the potential of image classification by a CNN or a capsule network to classify the state of dividing yeast cells (i.e. budded, unbudded, etc.) trapped in a microfluidic device (Ghafari et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ghafari et al., 2021.

claim: The previous CNN-based study has not demonstrated its ability to perform automated division counting or determine the RLS of individual cells due to limited accuracy of the model.
source: However, due to the limited accuracy of the model, it has not demonstrated its ability to perform an automated division counting, let alone determine the RLS of individual cells.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the previous study by Ghafari et al., 2021.

claim: The misclassification of a single frame during the lifespan can dramatically compromise the accuracy of the RLS measurement.
source: This is likely due to the fact that the misclassification of a single frame during the lifespan can dramatically compromise the accuracy of the RLS measurement.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about why previous methods failed.

claim: The microfluidic device features 16 independent chambers with 2000 traps each.
source: Altogether, the microfluidic device features 16 independent chambers with 2000 traps each, eliciting multiple conditions and strains to be analyzed in parallel.
evidence: This is a direct description of the device design.

claim: Small jaws were added on the top of the trap to better retain the mother cells in the traps.
source: Based on a design similar to that reported in previous studies (Jo et al., 2015; Crane et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2015), we added small jaws on the top of the trap to better retain the mother cells in the traps (especially the old ones Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The wall thickness of the traps was reduced to facilitate their deformation and avoid strong mechanical constraints when the cells become too big.
source: In addition, we reduced the wall thickness of the traps to facilitate their deformation and thus avoid strong mechanical constraints when the cells become too big (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,G and supplementary text for details).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,G.

claim: A microfluidic barrier was added that filters cells coming from microcolonies located upstream of the trap matrix.
source: Finally, we added a microfluidic barrier that filters cells coming from microcolonies located upstream of the trap matrix, which eventually clog the device and thus compromise the experiment after typically 24 h of culture.
evidence: This is stated as a design feature to prevent clogging.

claim: The custom benchtop microscope was built using simple optical parts for a total cost of fewer than 40 k euros.
source: For this, we used a simple rigid frame with inverted epifluorescence optics, a fixed dual-band GFP/mCherry filter set, a brightfield illumination column, a camera, and a motorized stage, for a total cost of fewer than 40 k euros (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with reference to the figure showing the setup.

claim: The minimal microscope allowed following the successive divisions and entry into senescence of typically 30,000 individual cells in parallel with a 5 min resolution.
source: Using a ×20 magnification objective, this 'minimal' microscope allowed us to follow the successive divisions and the entry into senescence of typically 30,000 individual cells in parallel with a 5 min resolution (knowing that there are ~500 traps per field of view using the ×20 objective).
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the imaging system.

claim: A convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the 'Inception v1' architecture was trained to predict the budding state of trapped cells by assigning one of six possible classes to each frame.
source: For this, we have trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the 'Inception v1' architecture (Szegedy et al., 2015) to predict the budding state of the trapped cells by assigning one of six possible classes (unbudded, small-budded, large-budded, dead, empty trap, and clogged trap) to each frame (Figure 2A, Top).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The alternation between the 'large budded' or 'unbudded' and the 'small budded' states reveals bud emergences.
source: In this framework, the alternation between the 'large budded' or 'unbudded' and the 'small budded' states reveals bud emergences.
evidence: This is stated as the logic for detecting cell divisions.

claim: The cell cycle durations can be deduced by measuring the time interval between successive budding events.
source: The cell cycle durations can be deduced by measuring the time interval between successive budding events, and the occurrence of the 'dead' class determines the end of the cell's lifespan (Figure 2A, Bottom).
evidence: This is stated as the method for calculating cell cycle durations.

claim: 250 traps were manually annotated to generate a groundtruth dataset for training and evaluating the classifier.
source: To train and evaluate the performance of the classifier, we generated a manually annotated dataset (referred to as 'groundtruth' in the following) by arbitrarily selecting 250 traps (split into a training and a test set, see Methods) containing situations representative of all cellular states from different fields of view and independent experimental replicates.
evidence: This is stated as the method for generating training data.

claim: The CNN model tends to predict 'ghost' divisions of abnormally short duration.
source: Despite a good visual match between the groundtruth and the CNN predictions, the distribution of cell-cycle durations revealed that the model tends to predict 'ghost' divisions of abnormally short duration (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the validation results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Sporadic misclassification could falsely assign a cell to the 'dead' state, thus decreasing the number of total generations predicted.
source: In addition, sporadic misclassification could falsely assign a cell to the 'dead' state, thus decreasing the number of total generations predicted based on the test dataset (N=1127 for the groundtruth versus N=804 for the CNN model, see Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the CNN model with supporting data in Figure 2C.

claim: The combined CNN+LSTM architecture provided the necessary robustness to provide an accurate prediction of individual cellular lifespan based on image sequence classification.
source: Altogether, these benchmarks indicated that only the combined CNN+LSTM architecture provided the necessary robustness to provide an accurate prediction of individual cellular lifespan based on image sequence classification.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the benchmarking experiments.

claim: Less than 3.5 s were necessary to classify the 1000 images in one lifespan using 8 Tesla K80 GPUs.
source: We were thus able to obtain a survival curve with N=1880 lifespans in a remarkably short time (Figure 2E): less than 3.5 s were necessary to classify the 1000 images in one lifespan using 8 Tesla K80 GPUs (see Methods for details).
evidence: This is stated as a performance metric of the system.

claim: Computing is ~100 times faster than manual annotation.
source: This is to be compared with manual annotation of images which takes 5–10 min per cell lifespan depending on the number of generations (i.e. computing is ~100 times faster than manual annotation).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between automated and manual analysis.

claim: It would have taken a human being between 7 and 14 days, working 24 h a day, to manually annotate 2000 cells (vs. 2 h for the computer).
source: Conversely, it would have taken a human being between 7 and 14 days, working 24 h a day, to manually annotate 2000 cells (vs. 2 h for the computer).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of time efficiency.

claim: The classification model recapitulated the increase in longevity observed in the fob1Δ mutant.
source: Remarkably, we recapitulated the increase (resp. decrease) in longevity observed in the fob1Δ (resp. sir2Δ) mutant (Defossez et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2000) and we could compute the related death rate with a high-confidence interval thanks to this large-scale dataset (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with citations to previous work and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The classification model recapitulated the decrease in longevity observed in the sir2Δ mutant.
source: Remarkably, we recapitulated the increase (resp. decrease) in longevity observed in the fob1Δ (resp. sir2Δ) mutant (Defossez et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2000) and we could compute the related death rate with a high-confidence interval thanks to this large-scale dataset (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with citations to previous work and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The median RLS was 26 generations for cells growing in glucose (N=1174 events).
source: In addition, using glucose and galactose as carbon sources, we performed comparative measurements of cell-cycle durations (N=38,205 events and N=15,495 events for glucose and galactose, see Figure 2F inset) and RLS (median = 26 generations, N=1174 events and median=24, N=565 events, for glucose and galactose, respectively, Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement result shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The median RLS was 24 generations for cells growing in galactose (N=565 events).
source: In addition, using glucose and galactose as carbon sources, we performed comparative measurements of cell-cycle durations (N=38,205 events and N=15,495 events for glucose and galactose, see Figure 2F inset) and RLS (median = 26 generations, N=1174 events and median=24, N=565 events, for glucose and galactose, respectively, Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement result shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The results were in line with previous measurements using glucose and galactose as carbon sources.
source: Our results were in line with previous measurements (Liu et al., 2015; Frenk et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to previous work with citations.

claim: The model initially trained with cells growing under glucose conditions could be successfully applied to data obtained with another carbon source (galactose).
source: This evaluation demonstrated that the model initially trained with cells growing under glucose conditions could be successfully applied to data obtained with another carbon source, which is known to affect the cell-cycle duration and the general physiology of the cell.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the validation experiments with galactose.

claim: The classification pipeline can successfully detect cell divisions, perform lifespan replicative analysis with high throughput, and is robust enough to be employed with different strain backgrounds and under various environmental conditions.
source: Altogether, our study shows that our classification pipeline can successfully detect cell divisions, perform lifespan replicative analysis with high throughput, and is robust enough to be employed with different strain backgrounds and under various environmental conditions, even though the training has only been performed on WT data and in glucose conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion from the validation experiments.

claim: A 'semi-open' geometry did not prevent large mother cells from being sporadically expelled during the budding of their daughters.
source: This analysis revealed that a 'semi-open' geometry (as in the design shown in Figure 3D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) did not prevent large mother cells from being sporadically expelled during the budding of their daughters, unlike other cell trap shapes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from retention rate analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Each specialist classifier performed very well on each specific test dataset.
source: The different benchmarks (i.e. classification performance and division predictions) showed that each specialist performed very well on each specific test dataset, thus confirming further that our analysis pipeline is robust and applicable to different cell trapping and imaging configurations.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparative analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: A unique 'generalist' classifier showed comparable performance to the different specialists.
source: Last, instead of training the classifiers separately on each dataset, we asked whether a unique classifier would have sufficient capacity to handle the pooled datasets with all imaging conditions and trap geometries used in Figure 3. Strikingly, this "generalist" model showed comparable performance to the different specialists.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparative analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Aging yeast cells undergo a cell-cycle slowdown when approaching senescence.
source: Aging yeast cells have long been reported to undergo a cell-cycle slowdown when approaching senescence (Mortimer and Johnson, 1959), a phenomenon that we have since quantified and referred to as the Senescence Entry Point or SEP (Fehrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The abrupt physiological decline in the cellular lifespan is concomitant with the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs).
source: More recently, we have demonstrated that this quite abrupt physiological decline in the cellular lifespan is concomitant with the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs) (Morlot et al., 2019), a long described marker of aging in yeast (Sinclair and Guarente, 1997).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: An LSTM sequence-to-sequence classifier was trained to assign a 'pre-SEP' or 'post-SEP' label to each frame.
source: Hence, to achieve a reliable determination of the SEP in an automated manner, we sought to develop an additional classification scheme as follows: we trained a simple LSTM sequence-to-sequence classifier to assign a 'pre-SEP' or 'post-SEP' label (before or after the SEP, respectively) to each frame, using the sequence of cellular state probabilities (i.e. the output of the CNN+LSTM image classifier described in Figure 2A) as input (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as the method for SEP detection shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The SEP transition could be successfully identified with R²=0.93.
source: Comparing the predictions to the groundtruth revealed that we could successfully identify the transition to a slow division mode (R²=0.93, see Figure 4B–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: The rapid increase in the average cell-cycle durations after aligning individual trajectories from the SEP transition could be recapitulated.
source: Hence, we could recapitulate the rapid increase in the average cell-cycle durations after aligning individual trajectories from that transition (Figure 4D), as described before (Fehrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 4D with citation to previous work.

claim: An encoder/decoder network based on the DeepLabV3+ architecture was used to segment brightfield images.
source: Here, since the complexity of images with individual cell traps is limited, we have used an encoder/decoder network based on the DeepLabV3+ architecture (Chen et al., 2018, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), to segment brightfield images (Figure 5A, Figure 5—video 1, and Methods).
evidence: This is stated as the method for semantic segmentation with citation and reference to figures.

claim: The model was trained on ~1,400 manually segmented brightfield images using three output classes.
source: We trained the model on ~1,400 manually segmented brightfield images using three output classes (i.e. 'background,' 'mother cell,' 'other cell') in order to discriminate the mother cell of interest from the surrounding cellular objects.
evidence: This is stated as the training procedure for the segmentation model.

claim: Mother cell contours could be determined accurately with a trained classifier.
source: Our results revealed that mother cell contours could be determined accurately with a trained classifier (Figure 5A–C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-D).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 5A-C and supplementary figures.

claim: The segmentation procedure allowed quantifying the dynamics of volume increase of the mother cell during replicative aging.
source: Overall, this segmentation procedure allowed us to quantify the dynamics of volume increase of the mother cell during replicative aging (Figure 5C–D), as previously reported (Morlot et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 5C-D with citation to previous work.

claim: A similar training procedure with ~3000 fluorescence images with a nuclear marker yielded accurate nuclei contours.
source: Last, a similar training procedure with ~3000 fluorescence images with a nuclear marker (using a strain carrying a histone-Neongreen fusion) yielded accurate nuclei contours (Figure 5E–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 5E-F and supplementary figure.

claim: The segmentation successfully recapitulated the sharp burst in nuclear fluorescence that follows the Senescence Entry Point.
source: It successfully recapitulated the sharp burst in nuclear fluorescence that follows the Senescence Entry Point (Figure 5G–H; Morlot et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 5G-H with citation to previous work.

claim: Young cells were abruptly exposed to different stress concentrations, ranging from 0 to 0.8 mM H2O2, and observed over about 15 h.
source: For this purpose, young cells were abruptly exposed to different stress concentrations, ranging from 0 to 0.8 mM H2O2, and observed over about 15 h (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as the experimental design shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A strain carrying the Tsa1-GFP fusion protein was used as a fluorescent reporter of the cellular response to oxidative stress.
source: We used a strain carrying the Tsa1-GFP fusion protein (TSA1 encodes a peroxiredoxin, a major cytosolic antioxidant overexpressed in response to oxidative stress) as a fluorescent reporter of the cellular response to this stress (Goulev et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as the experimental design with citation to previous work.

claim: The automated analysis revealed different possible cell fates, whose proportions varied according to the stress concentration.
source: Our automated analysis revealed different possible cell fates, whose proportions varied according to the stress concentration (Figure 6A and B)
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: In the absence of stress (0 mM), cells maintained a constant division rate throughout the experiment.
source: in the absence of stress (0 mM), cells maintained a constant division rate throughout the experiment
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the stress response experiments.

claim: At 0.3 mM H2O2, the population partitioned between cells that recovered a normal division rate after experiencing a delay and others that seemed unable to resume a normal cell-cycle.
source: in contrast, at 0.3 mM, the population partitioned between cells that recovered a normal division rate after experiencing a delay (see the 'adapted cells' in Figure 6B) and others that seemed unable to resume a normal cell-cycle (see the 'slowly dividing cells' in Figure 6B), in agreement with previous results (Goulev et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the stress response experiments shown in Figure 6B with citation to previous work.

claim: Higher doses of stress (0.5 mM and 0.8 mM) saw adapted and slowly dividing populations gradually disappear, indicating that very few divisions occur at these elevated doses.
source: Higher doses of stress (0.5 mM and 0.8 mM) saw these populations gradually disappear, indicating that very few divisions occur at these elevated doses.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the stress response experiments.

claim: The analysis revealed a progressive, dose-dependent increase in the fraction of dead cells over time.
source: Our analysis revealed a progressive, dose-dependent increase in the fraction of dead cells over time, which was confirmed by a comparison between groundtruth data and network predictions of the time of cell death (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 6C and validated in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The population-averaged mean cytoplasmic fluorescence revealed a significant increase at 0.3 mM H2O2 due to the transcriptional upregulation of antioxidant genes.
source: The population-averaged mean cytoplasmic fluorescence revealed a significant increase at 0.3 mM H2O2 due to the transcriptional upregulation of antioxidant genes, as previously described (Goulev et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a result with citation to previous work.

claim: The average upregulation of Tsa1 was lessened at higher doses, an effect attributed to the large fraction of cell death observed in these conditions.
source: However, this average upregulation of Tsa1 was lessened at higher doses, an effect we attribute to the large fraction of cell death observed in these conditions (e.g.: bottom cell in Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results shown in Figure 6.

claim: DetecDiv used with single-cell traps provides a highly suitable method for quantifying both cell division rate and mortality in real-time under variable environmental conditions.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that DetecDiv used with single-cell traps provides a highly suitable method for quantifying both cell division rate and mortality in real-time under variable environmental conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the stress response experiments.

claim: The pipeline combines the use of two architectures: a CNN+LSTM network for the exploitation of temporal information and semantic segmentation (DeepLabV3+) for the quantification of spatial information.
source: In this study, we have developed a pipeline based on the combined use of two architectures, namely a CNN+LSTM network for the exploitation of temporal information and semantic segmentation (DeepLabV3+) for the quantification of spatial information.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the methodology.

claim: The pipeline can successfully characterize the dynamics of multi-generational phenomena, using the example of the entry into replicative senescence in yeast.
source: We demonstrate that it can successfully characterize the dynamics of multi-generational phenomena, using the example of the entry into replicative senescence in yeast, a difficult case study that has long resisted any automated analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the results.

claim: The classification model was successfully used to score cellular adaptation and mortality in the context of the physiological stress response to hydrogen peroxide.
source: We also successfully used our classification model to score cellular adaptation and mortality in the context of the physiological stress response to hydrogen peroxide.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the stress response experiments.

claim: A graphical user interface was developed to make this method accessible for the community without requiring any programming knowledge.
source: Furthermore, we have developed a graphical user interface to make this method accessible for the community without requiring any programming knowledge.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of the DetecDiv software.

claim: The methodology will unleash the potential of microfluidic cell trapping devices to quantify temporal physiological metrics in a high-throughput and single-cell manner.
source: We envision that this methodology will unleash the potential of microfluidic cell trapping devices to quantify temporal physiological metrics in a high-throughput and single-cell manner.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about future applications.

claim: The major novelty of this work lies in the development of an analysis method to automatically obtain survival curves and cytometric measurements during the entry into senescence from raw image sequences.
source: The major novelty of this work lies in the development of an analysis method to automatically obtain survival curves and cytometric measurements during the entry into senescence from raw image sequences.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the contribution.

claim: The cost of an hour of microscopy is around 10–20 euros in an imaging facility.
source: Although many laboratories use common imaging platforms with shared equipment, it is important to note that the cost of an hour of microscopy is around 10–20 euros in an imaging facility.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about facility costs.

claim: An RLS assay typically lasts 60–80 hours.
source: As an RLS assay typically lasts 60–80 hours, these experiments may not be affordable.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about RLS assay duration.

claim: The analysis pipeline works perfectly even with a low optical resolution (the theoretical resolution of the imaging system with a ×20, N.A. 0.45 objective is ~0.7 µm).
source: Using this experimental setup, we showed that our analysis pipeline works perfectly even with a low optical resolution (i.e. the theoretical resolution of our imaging system with a ×20, N.A. 0.45 objective is ~0.7 µm), and without any contrast-enhancing method.
evidence: This is stated as a result demonstrating the robustness of the method.

claim: DetecDiv works similarly with higher magnification objectives and different imaging systems.
source: Yet, using the same microfluidic device described here, we showed that DetecDiv works similarly with higher magnification objectives and different imaging systems.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the comparative analysis.

claim: Division detection can be performed with cells growing in traps with different geometries.
source: In addition, we demonstrated that division detection can also be performed with cells growing in traps with different geometries (Figure 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 3 and supplementary figures.

claim: A unique classifier trained on a large collection of images obtained under broad imaging contexts can achieve accurate division detection.
source: Furthermore, a unique classifier trained on a large collection of images obtained under broad imaging contexts can also achieve accurate division detection.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the generalist classifier experiments.

claim: The accuracy of RLS measurements may be affected when using designs with a low retention rate.
source: However, one limitation to applying our analysis pipeline with a broad range of trap geometries is that the accuracy of RLS measurements may be affected when using designs with a low retention rate.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: The method is currently unable to systematically detect when a mother cell is replaced by its daughter.
source: Although lifespan trajectories can be marked as 'censored' when the mother cell leaves the traps (as proposed in a recently released preprint Thayer et al., 2022), our method is currently unable to systematically detect when a mother cell is replaced by its daughter (e.g. cell traps in Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method with reference to a figure.

claim: Retention is an essential feature to consider when designing the geometry of a trap.
source: Therefore, we believe that retention is an essential feature to consider when designing the geometry of a trap.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the retention analysis.

claim: Individual cell trapping behaves as a 'hardware-based cell tracking' method, thus alleviating the need to identify and track objects spatially.
source: An important advantage of individual cell trapping is that it makes image analysis much simpler than using chambers filled with two-dimensional cell microcolonies. Indeed, individual traps behave as a 'hardware-based cell tracking' method, thus alleviating the need to identify and track objects spatially, a procedure that provides an additional source of errors.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the trap-based approach.

claim: The specific state of the few cells surrounding the mother may not influence the reliability of the classification of the mother.
source: Because the cells of interest are located in the middle of the traps, the learning process can focus the attention of the classifier on the state of the mother cell only (e.g. small-budded, large-budded, etc.), hence the specific state of the few cells surrounding it may not influence the reliability of the classification of the mother (Figure 2—figure supplement 3 for specific examples).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Whole image classification can easily be coupled to a recurrent neural network (such as an LSTM network), thus opening the door to more accurate analyses that exploit temporal dependencies between images.
source: In addition, a powerful feature of whole image classification is that it can easily be coupled to a recurrent neural network (such as an LSTM network), thus opening the door to more accurate analyses that exploit temporal dependencies between images, as demonstrated in our study.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the approach demonstrated in the study.

claim: A limitation of the classification scheme is that the buds that arise from the mother cell can not be identified.
source: However, a limitation of our classification scheme is that the buds that arise from the mother cell can not be identified, and further work is necessary to assess the requirements (e.g. the size of the training set) to achieve their successful segmentation, such as using a separate 'bud' class.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current method.

claim: It is currently impossible to measure the growth rate (in volume) of the mother cell over time.
source: Thus, it is currently impossible to measure the growth rate (in volume) of the mother cell over time (most of the biomass created during the budded period goes into the bud) and it precludes analyzing fluorescent markers that would localize into the bud.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation resulting from the inability to segment buds.

claim: The division counting/lifespan reconstruction classifier can readily be used to quantify cellular dynamics and mortality in response to hydrogen peroxide stress.
source: Here, we show that our division counting/lifespan reconstruction classifier can readily be used to quantify cellular dynamics and mortality in response to hydrogen peroxide stress.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the stress response experiments.

claim: DetecDiv could be further applied in different contexts without additional development, yet with potential retraining of the classifier with complementary data, and/or following the definition of new classes.
source: We envision that DetecDiv could be further applied in different contexts without additional development - yet with potential retraining of the classifier with complementary data, and/or following the definition of new classes.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about future applications.

claim: The rationalization of division rate measurements in a system where there is no competition between cells offers a unique framework to study the heterogeneity of cell behaviors in response to environmental changes.
source: More generally, the rationalization of division rate measurements in a system where there is no competition between cells offers a unique framework to study the heterogeneity of cell behaviors in response to environmental changes (stress, chemical drugs, etc.), as demonstrated in our study and evidenced by the rise of high-throughput quantitative studies in bacteria (Bakshi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a general advantage of the approach with citation to related work.

claim: Mechanistic studies of the cell-cycle could benefit from a precise and standardized phenotypic characterization of the division dynamics.
source: Mechanistic studies of the cell-cycle could also benefit from a precise and standardized phenotypic characterization of the division dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about potential applications.

claim: The approach described here may be easily transferred to other cellular models to characterize heterogeneous and complex temporal patterns in biological signals.
source: We envision that the kind of approach described here may be easily transferred to other cellular models to characterize heterogeneous and complex temporal patterns in biological signals.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about future applications to other systems.

claim: 94% of the cells that underwent at least five divisions in the trap would stay inside until their death.
source: We have measured that 94% of the cells that underwent at least five divisions in the trap would stay inside until their death.
evidence: This is stated as a measurement of trap retention rate.

claim: The F1-score was found to be higher than 85% for all classes in the CNN classifier.
source: The F1-score was found to be higher than 85% for all classes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The combined CNN+LSTM network achieved about 90–95% precision and recall for all classes.
source: We obtained only a marginal increase in the classification metrics compared to the CNN network (about 90–95% precision and recall for all classes, see Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: The difference between the number of generations predicted by the CNN+LSTM network and the actual number was less than 2%.
source: and the difference between the number of generations predicted by the network and the actual number was less than 2% (N=1147 and N=1127, respectively, see left panel on Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The Pearson correlation coefficient for groundtruth vs prediction of cell-cycle durations was R²=0.996.
source: In addition, the Pearson correlation coefficient for groundtruth vs prediction was very high (R²=0.996, see right panel on Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The predicted survival curve was almost identical to that computed from the groundtruth (p=0.74).
source: Similarly, the predicted survival curve was almost identical to that computed from the groundtruth (p=0.74, Figure 2D and Figure 2—video 1) and the corresponding Pearson correlation reached 0.991 (vs 0.8 and 0.1 for the CNN+PP and CNN, respectively).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The Pearson correlation for predicted vs groundtruth lifespans reached 0.991 for the CNN+LSTM network.
source: Similarly, the predicted survival curve was almost identical to that computed from the groundtruth (p=0.74, Figure 2D and Figure 2—video 1) and the corresponding Pearson correlation reached 0.991 (vs 0.8 and 0.1 for the CNN+PP and CNN, respectively).
evidence: This is stated as a benchmarking result shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A survival curve with N=1880 lifespans was obtained.
source: We were thus able to obtain a survival curve with N=1880 lifespans in a remarkably short time (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is stated as a result shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The median RLS for wild-type cells was 26 generations (N=1880).
source: We were thus able to obtain a survival curve with N=1880 lifespans in a remarkably short time (Figure 2E)
evidence: This can be inferred from Figure 2E which shows the survival curve for WT cells.

claim: The median RLS for fob1Δ mutant was 38 generations (N=2531).
source: Remarkably, we recapitulated the increase (resp. decrease) in longevity observed in the fob1Δ (resp. sir2Δ) mutant (Defossez et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2000) and we could compute the related death rate with a high-confidence interval thanks to this large-scale dataset (Figure 2E).
evidence: This can be inferred from Figure 2E which shows the survival curve for fob1Δ mutant.

claim: The median RLS for sir2Δ mutant was 12 generations (N=1264).
source: Remarkably, we recapitulated the increase (resp. decrease) in longevity observed in the fob1Δ (resp. sir2Δ) mutant (Defossez et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2000) and we could compute the related death rate with a high-confidence interval thanks to this large-scale dataset (Figure 2E).
evidence: This can be inferred from Figure 2E which shows the survival curve for sir2Δ mutant.

claim: The microfluidic device has a retention rate of 94% for cells that undergo at least five divisions.
source: We have measured that 94% of the cells that underwent at least five divisions in the trap would stay inside until their death.
evidence: This is stated as a measurement of the trap performance.

claim: The retention rate of the new trap design (94%) is higher than the classical trap design (59%).
source: We have measured that 94% of the cells that underwent at least five divisions in the trap would stay inside until their death. This is striking contrast with the results obtained with a device with a semi-open trap geometry (see Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 for details).
evidence: This can be inferred from the comparison shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.
